reason: The text from Judges 4 demonstrates multiple instances of Hebrew people freely expressing their views without discouragement. The Israelites cry out to the Lord with their distress (וַיִּצְעֲקוּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל־ יְהוָ֑ה). Deborah openly prophesies and gives commands to Barak. Most significantly, Barak directly negotiates conditions with Deborah, stating he will only go if she accompanies him (אִם־ תֵּלְכִ֥י עִמִּ֖י וְהָלָ֑כְתִּי), and Deborah responds to his condition. The text depicts open dialogue, communication, and the expression of concerns and desires by the Hebrew people, with no indication of discouragement from expressing views.
